node.title: Re: Hex value of Perl file handle to uniquely identify
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [eyepopslikeamosquito],

There's also [doc://fileno], but those numbers are re-used. I don't have much experience with [doc://fileno], so perhaps a monk who does can say more, but I imagine that if you closely keep track of when filehandles are closed, you could still use [doc://fileno] to tell different connections apart.

open my $fh1, '<', '/tmp/foo' or die $!; open my $fh2, '<', '/tmp/bar' or die $!; print "fh1: ", fileno($fh1), "\n"; print "fh2: ", fileno($fh2), "\n"; __END__ fh1: 3 fh2: 4

Otherwise, I agree with [BrowserUk]: a good way to identify network connections is by properties like remote IP + remote port.

A while back I tried out [mod://POE]. Its API takes quite a bit of getting used to, but once you've got the hang of it, it works well. Since each "session" has a unique ID, keeping track of clients is easy. The [http://poe.perl.org/?POE_Cookbook/TCP_Servers|Cookbook] is really helpful in getting started.

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
